text-1mib.why: 1 MiB of paragraphs, 264 pages: each page leaves memory once written, so the account peaks near 2 MiB and the process near 60 MiB.

text-4mib.why: 4 MiB of paragraphs, about 1,050 pages: each page leaves memory once written, so the account peaks near 8 MiB and the process near 90 MiB.

text-16mib.why: 16 MiB of paragraphs, the default input cap, about 4,200 pages: each page leaves memory once written, so the account peaks near 20 MiB, the source and the output streams it keeps past the spool threshold, and the process near 220 MiB.

html-1mib.why: 1 MiB of paragraphs, 257 pages: the account holds about 135 MiB at its peak, the Go heap about 300 MiB.

html-4mib.why: 4 MiB of paragraphs, about 1,025 pages: the account holds about 540 MiB at its peak, the process about 1.2 GiB.

html-16mib.why: 16 MiB of paragraphs: the glyph runs of the laid-out lines alone would hold over 1 GiB, and the budget refuses them during the layout. The shaped paragraphs are given back to the account as the flow settles, so the refusal comes once the lines themselves pass the budget, and the process peaks near 1.4 GiB, under twice the budget.

html-png-10.why: Ten distinct 12-megapixel PNGs: each is held decoded, 48 MB, only while it is encoded, then its compressed samples go to the conversion's picture file past 8 MiB; the account peaks near 55 MiB, the process near 280 MiB.

html-png-50.why: Fifty distinct 12-megapixel PNGs, 2.4 GB of pixels decoded one at a time, their compressed samples kept in the conversion's picture file past 8 MiB: the account peaks near 65 MiB and the Go heap near 230 MiB, where both held the samples, 310 MiB, before.

html-jpeg-10.why: Ten distinct 12-megapixel JPEGs, written as they are: their files are charged, no pixel is decoded.

html-jpeg-50.why: Fifty distinct 12-megapixel JPEGs, written as they are: the first 8 MiB of their files are held and charged, the rest wait in the conversion's picture file; no pixel is decoded.

csv-100k.why: 100,000 cells, about 190 pages: each page leaves memory once written, but every cell is charged when it is read, so the account still peaks near 160 MiB; the process peaks near 280 MiB.

csv-1000k.why: 1,000,000 cells, the cap: each cell is charged what the pages built from it cost when it is read, so the budget refuses the workbook while it is read, before any page is planned.

html-frames-self.why: A page framing itself fifty times, and two documents framing each other: a document appears once among the documents that frame it, so each frame of the page shows it once, with empty frames inside, and the pair alternates until frames nest 8 deep; about 70 MiB.

html-frames-chain-200.why: 200 documents, each framing the next: frames nest 8 deep, so the documents 0 to 7 show and the ninth level is left out with a warning, its box empty; about 50 MiB.

html-frames-10000.why: 10,000 frames of one document of 1 MiB of paragraphs: the document is read once, and the documents the frames lay out are held together to the input cap of 16 MiB, so 16 frames show it and the others keep their boxes empty, with a warning; about 830 pages, 7 seconds and 360 MiB.

docx-2000pages.why: 2,000 pages of one paragraph each: the account holds about 160 MiB at its peak, the Go heap about 370 MiB.

pptx-500slides.why: 500 slides of a title and a paragraph on one master: each page leaves memory once written, so the account peaks near 9 MiB and the process near 70 MiB.
